To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the autonomic nervous system is the common link between stress and functional syndrome.
the autonomic nervous system is a key factor in the development of stress and that autonomic nervous system assessment is an essential tool in the clinical approach of functional syndromes.
the combination of a multidimensional clinical approach with the use of a new technology, the autonomic assessment, provides an efficient and safe treatment of stress and functional syndrome.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and treatment of stress related functional syndromes in clinical practice.
the identification of new diagnostic and therapeutic approaches in the field of functional syndromes, in which stress plays an important role.
the development of a new approach to stress and functional syndrome, based on the integration of behavioral therapy and autonomic assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stress and functional syndrome represent two different faces of the same coin.
stress is an essential element in the pathogenesis of functional syndromes, and that the latter are a major source of stress for patients, doctors and society.

functional syndromes are not only the expression of psychosomatic mechanisms, but also of an altered neuroendocrine control of the cardiovascular system, with the possibility of a better understanding of their pathophysiology and a more effective management.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the treatment of patients with functional syndromes requires a multidimensional approach including behavioral therapy and pharmacology, guided by a more complete diagnostic process.

the new tools of non invasive assessment of autonomic function provide a more objective and quantitative support to the clinical evaluation of patients with functional syndromes, allowing a more effective and personalized management.
the treatment of stress related symptoms is a challenge to be addressed with a multidimensional approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the mechanisms of stress and of functional syndromes may help clinicians to provide a more effective treatment.
a more complete approach of functional syndromes may help in the prevention of chronic diseases, including cardiovascular ones, and improve quality of life of patients.
the treatment of functional syndromes is not only a challenge but also a fascinating opportunity to develop an integrative approach to the patient, with an active role for the internist.
